## Background

Breast cancer is biologically heterogeneous.

Breast Cancer patients may differ in:

  - Hormone-related signaling
  
  - Tumor growth and proliferation
  
  - DNA repair mechanisms
  
  - Cellular signaling pathways
  
  - Immune-related activity

Difference in biology may create differences in clinical characteristics and prognosis.

## Gene expression

- If treat DNA as the factory

- Gene is the guildance

- Expression is the level of using this guildance (gene) to generate the product (protein)

## Cancer pathway

- A pathway (biological pathway) is a series or network of biological activities in which multiple genes or proteins participate to carry out a specific function within a cell.

## Cancer pathway

- Some pathways in breast cancer

  - Estrogen / hormone signaling: how cells respond to hormones.
  
  - PI3K–AKT–mTOR signaling: how cells receive and transmit signals for growth/survival.
  
  - Cell cycle / proliferation: how rapidly or slowly cells divide. 
  
  - DNA repair: how cells repair damaged DNA.

## Research question

Do breast cancer **subgroups** identified through pathway-informed gene expression **clustering** differ in clinical characteristics and overall survival?

## Data

[METABRIC data](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/raghadalharbi/breast-cancer-gene-expression-profiles-metabric/data){target="_blank"} include:

  - Clinical variables
  
  - m-RNA levels z-score (gene expression)
  
  - genes mutations

for 1904 patients breast cancer patient

## Methodology for preliminary analysis

- Biological pathway selection

- Gene mapping

- Coverage assessment 

- Pathway scoring & patient clustering

- Unsupervised clustering to create 2 subgroups

## Survival analysis

- Clinical characterization & survival analysis between those subgroups

- Cox proportional hazard regression
